what: The queue worker did not finish startup within the configured timeout.
fix: Check Redis connectivity and worker context creation; raise startupTimeoutMs only when startup legitimately needs longer.

what: The queue worker was started while already running.
fix: Start the app once, or stop the queue worker before starting it again.

what: The queue worker was stopped before successful startup.
fix: Stop only after successful startup or let the Dot lifecycle manage shutdown.

what: A job, schedule or flow definition has no name.
fix: Give the job, schedule or flow a non-empty name before building its definition.

what: A handler was declared before its input schema.
fix: Call .input(schema) before defining the handler or building the declaration.

what: A flow definition has no steps.
fix: Add at least one .step(...) before building a flow.

what: A flow step depends on an undeclared step.
fix: Reference only step ids declared in the same flow.

what: Flow step dependencies contain a cycle.
fix: Remove dependency cycles so the flow steps form a directed acyclic graph.

what: A cron interval or time is outside its supported range.
fix: Pass cron intervals and times within the helper limits stated by the error.

what: A schedule wrapping a job declares schedule-level middleware.
fix: Remove schedule-level .use() when wrapping a job; put middleware on the job instead.

what: Two schedules use the same name.
fix: Give each schedule a distinct .name(...), including schedules wrapping the same job.

what: The job changed since the preview the approval pinned (it failed again, or was touched). HTTP 409.
fix: Refresh the failed-job preview and obtain approval for its current revision.

what: The job is no longer failed: it was already re-queued, or it is gone. HTTP 409.
fix: Refresh the job state and select an existing failed job before retrying.

what: The module has no queue under that key. HTTP 404.
fix: Use a queue key registered by the module.

what: A flow step has more than one dependent.
fix: Reshape the flow so a step has at most one dependent; use a supported dependency tree.

what: The enqueue input does not satisfy the flow input schema.
fix: Pass enqueue input accepted by the declared flow input schema.

what: Queue worker startup has no mounted queue client.
fix: Mount queue({ connection }) before feature registration and queueWorker startup.

what: A job name contains characters unsupported by the queue backend.
fix: Rename the job with only letters, digits and _ - . / (for example "orders.process"); a job name is its queue name, and BullMQ and pg-boss reject other characters such as ":".

what: An outbox write was attempted outside the business transaction.
fix: Call runAfter or runAt inside db.transaction and pass the business transaction handle.

what: The outbox arguments do not satisfy the job input schema.
fix: Pass args accepted by the job input schema; inspect the private schema issues.

what: The outbox delay, scheduled time or priority is invalid.
fix: Use a non-negative safe-integer delay, a valid runAt Date and a supported QUEUE_PRIORITIES value.

what: Stored outbox arguments do not satisfy the registered job input schema.
fix: Repair the stored args or restore the matching job schema before retrying the dead row; version job names when inputs change.

what: An outbox row names a job absent from the runner registry.
fix: Register the job in the registry used to construct the outbox runner.

what: Two jobs in the outbox registry use the same name.
fix: Give each job in the outbox registry a unique name.

what: The queue could not confirm whether the job was accepted.
fix: Inspect the job by its idempotency key before enqueueing it again.

what: The job has no active queue transport.
fix: Register and start the queue before triggering this job.

what: The queue worker started in the background and failed (Redis down, a slow start, a context factory that threw), so no job runs.
fix: Check Redis connectivity and the worker context factory, then restart the app; use `blocking: true` to fail `app.start()` instead.
